original_question: For the 1993 model with state variables p0,i(x,t), p1,i(x,t), p2(x,u,t), p3(x,t), and p4(x,u,t), representing a two-unit parallel system with operating, repair, waiting-for-repair, and suspended-repair states; with a1 > 0 the Erlang-distribution parameter, a2(x) the repair rate of unit 1, b1(x) the life rate, b2(x) the repair rate of unit 2, and boundary data including p0,1(0,t) = integral from 0 to infinity of p1,1(x,t) b2(x) dx + delta(t), determine whether the PDE model is well posed and determine the asymptotic behavior of its time-dependent solution.
target_in_paper: The draft is closest to the paper's unresolved general-case problem for the 1993 two-unit parallel reliability PDE with Dirac-delta boundary/initial data: after the paper solves the constant-rate special case and reformulates the general case via Laplace transform and an abstract Cauchy problem with an evolution-family operator, the remaining task is to establish well-posedness and describe the long-time asymptotic behavior of the time-dependent solution for the original model.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the specific 1993 two-unit parallel repair model, the relevant state-density unknowns p0,i(x,t), p1,i(x,t), p2(x,u,t), p3(x,t), p4(x,u,t), the presence of Dirac-delta boundary data, representative rate functions/parameters, and the two research tasks that fit the paper's open-problem direction: well-posedness and asymptotic behavior of the time-dependent solution.
missing_details: It should explicitly say that the question is about the general-coefficient version of the 1993 model, because the paper states that the constant-rate special case is already solved.
It should state that the model is a coupled first-order PDE system with Dirac-delta terms in both boundary and initial conditions, not just list one boundary relation.
It should specify the underlying domains of the state variables: x >= 0, u >= 0, t >= 0, and which unknowns live on [0, infinity) versus [0, infinity)^2.

It should define what 'well posed' means in the paper's setting: existence, uniqueness, and continuous dependence of the time-dependent solution in an appropriate Banach-space formulation of the abstract Cauchy problem.
It should identify the functional-analytic reformulation that the paper uses, namely the abstract Cauchy problem whose underlying operator is an evolution family.
It should make explicit whether the asymptotic question is the long-time behavior as t -> infinity of the full time-dependent solution, rather than just of a scalar reliability index.

It should include the full PDE system and all boundary/initial conditions if the question is meant to be fully stand-alone; the current draft gives only the state variables, rates, and one sample boundary condition.

It should specify the standing assumptions on the coefficient functions/rates (for example measurability, nonnegativity, and any boundedness/integrability conditions actually imposed in the model) if one wants a fully paper-faithful standalone statement.
It should note that no ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency data are relevant here; the missing structure is analytic, not algebraic.
refined_question: For the 1993 two-unit parallel reliability model described by a coupled system of first-order partial differential equations with state densities p0,i(x,t), p1,i(x,t), p2(x,u,t), p3(x,t), and p4(x,u,t), with x,u,t >= 0, rate data a1 > 0, a2(x), b1(x), b2(x), and boundary/initial conditions containing Dirac-delta terms (including relations of the form p0,1(0,t) = integral from 0 to infinity of p1,1(x,t)b2(x)dx + delta(t)), determine in the general-coefficient case whether the model is well posed in the paper's abstract-Cauchy-problem/evolution-family formulation, and determine the long-time asymptotic behavior as t -> infinity of its time-dependent solution.
justification: From the accessible primary-source text, the paper itself states three key facts: it studies a reliability/scheduling PDE system with Dirac-delta boundary and initial conditions; it completely handles only the special case in which the relevant rates are constants, obtaining explicit time-dependent solutions and their asymptotic behavior; and in the general case it only derives the Laplace transform and an abstract Cauchy problem whose underlying operator is an evolution family, before leaving open problems. That makes your draft align not with a solved theorem, but with the paper's unresolved general-case program. The draft is already substantially on target, but to be fully stand-alone and faithful it must say that the constant-rate case is excluded, define the solution framework for well-posedness, and clarify that the asymptotic question concerns the full time-dependent solution as t tends to infinity. I could verify this target from the arXiv abstract, but I could not recover a numbered open-problem label or PDF page from the full paper text through the available web interface.
